course_name_original: Técnicas de búsqueda y uso de la información (14155)

learning_outcomes.text: Will understand the need to locate and use reliable and trustworthy sources, and the importance of research based on digital information resources.
Will know the main information sources, both general and specialized in their discipline, identifying and selecting the most appropriate ones for each task.
Will identify information needs and develop effective strategies to locate appropriate sources and resources.
Will determine the reliability and quality of information and its sources.
Will retrieve information through precise and effective searches.
Will consider the ethical use of information and avoid plagiarism by knowing and mastering academic and deontological regulations and conventions.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other information sources.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Use different methods to communicate effectively with the engineering community and society in general.
Recognize the need and have the ability to voluntarily develop continuous learning.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.

That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to organize and plan their work, making correct decisions based on available information, gathering and interpreting relevant data to make judgments within their area of study.
Motivation and ability to engage in autonomous lifelong learning, allowing them to adapt to new situations.

syllabus_topics: Principles and strategies for efficient information retrieval in the digital environment.
Knowledge and use of the main platforms and access routes to digital information resources: general and specialized.
Tools for information organization and bibliographic management.
Ethical use of information and intellectual property regulations.
Creating and managing citations and bibliographic references in academic works.
How to present and order bibliographic references.
Automatic originality analysis tools for plagiarism prevention.
teaching_methods: Practices (case studies, problem solving, information search tasks)

assessment_methods.method: Formative assessment (practical exercises and self-assessment questionnaires, exercises and practical activities)

assessment_rules: The formative assessment, including practical exercises and self-assessment questionnaires, accounts for 70% of the final grade. A final test, conducted on the last day of class, accounts for 30%. A minimum score of 4.0 in the final test is required to pass the subject. Attendance and class participation may contribute to the final grade. There is a single call for this transversal subject, with all assessment tests during the teaching period. Students who do not pass may retake if they attended at least 75% of classes and submitted at least 75% of continuous assessment activities, by completing a multiple-choice test (50%) and a practical assignment (50%). Copying or plagiarism will result in a total loss of the activity's grade.
